text: Right, and that's expected: no backup has ever run. Two steps are missing, both yours, because my permissions can't create the passphrase for you or schedule tasks on your machine. In a Windows terminal: (1) Create C:\Users\Andre\.spirit-backup-passphrase with a passphrase of 12+ characters, and keep a copy somewhere safe. (2) Run once by hand to see a file appear: node D:\SpiritOS\install\backup-windows\backup.js (3) Then schedule it hourly: schtasks /Create /SC HOURLY /TN "SpiritOS backup" /TR "D:\SpiritOS\install\backup-windows\run.cmd" After step 2 a file named spirit-backup-<date>.tgz.enc is in that folder.

wsl-claude: checked from here, and that's expected: nothing has run yet. The folder exists and is empty; there's NO passphrase file in any C:\Users\*\ (.spirit-backup-passphrase), and NO scheduled task with 'spirit' in its name. The backup refuses to run without a passphrase, by design: there's never an unencrypted backup. Your two steps: (1) create %USERPROFILE%\.spirit-backup-passphrase with a passphrase of 12+ characters, and keep a copy somewhere that is NOT that Drive; (2) run the schtasks line from install/backup-windows/README.txt, or tell claude-windows 'schedule it'. The first file appears within the hour after that.
